title.zh: 卷四百〇五 列傳第一百六十四 李宗勉 袁甫 劉黻 王居安
title.en: Volume 405 Biographies 164: Li Zongmian, Yuan Fu, Liu Fu, Wang Juan
title.raw: 卷四百〇五 列傳第一百六十四 李宗勉 袁甫 劉黻 王居安 Volume 405 Biographies 164: Li Zongmian, Yuan Fu, Liu Fu, Wang Juan

sentences.zh: 李宗勉 袁甫 劉黻 王居安

translations.literal: Li Zongmian, Yuan Fu, Liu Fu, Wang Juan
translations.idiomatic: Li Zongmian, Yuan Fu, Liu Fu, and Wang Juan

sentences.zh: 李宗勉

translations.literal: Li Zongmian
translations.idiomatic: Li Zongmian

sentences.zh: 李宗勉，字強父，富陽人。

translations.literal: Li Zongmian, style name Qiangfu, was a native of Fuyang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zongmian, courtesy name Qiangfu, came from Fuyang.

sentences.zh: 開禧元年進士。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaixi he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the first year of the Kaixi reign (1205).

sentences.zh: 曆黃州教授、浙西茶鹽司、江西轉運司幹官。

translations.literal: He successively served as professor at Huang Prefecture, in the Zhexi Tea and Salt Commission, and as a staff officer in the Jiangxi Transport Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He held posts in turn as professor at Huang Prefecture, in the Zhexi Tea and Salt Commission, and as a staff officer of the Jiangxi Transport Commission.

sentences.zh: 嘉定十四年，主管吏部架閣，尋改太學正。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Jiading he was put in charge of the Ministry of Personnel archives; soon after he was made director of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Jiading (1221) he supervised the Ministry of Personnel archives, and shortly thereafter became director of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 明年爲博士，又明年遷國子博士。

translations.literal: The next year he became a erudite; the year after that he was promoted to erudite of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was appointed erudite, and the year after that promoted to erudite of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 寶慶初，添差通判嘉興府。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Baoqing he was given an additional assignment as vice-prefect of Jiaxing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Baoqing era (1225) he received an additional posting as vice-prefect of Jiaxing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 三年，召爲秘書郎。

translations.literal: In the third year he was summoned to serve as secretary in the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Baoqing he was called to the capital as a secretary in the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 紹定元年，遷著作郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaoding he was transferred to compiler in the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shaoding (1228) he was promoted to compiler in the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 入對，言邊事宜夙夜震懼，以消咎殃。

translations.literal: On audience he spoke of frontier affairs, saying one should be in dread day and night to dispel calamity.
translations.idiomatic: At an imperial audience he urged that border affairs be met with constant vigilance day and night, so that disaster might be averted.

sentences.zh: 明年，兼權兵部郎官。

translations.literal: The next year he was concurrently given acting charge as a bureau director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was concurrently appointed acting director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 時李全叛謀已露，人莫敢言，宗勉獨累疏及之。

translations.literal: At the time Li Quan's plot to rebel had already come to light, yet no one dared speak of it; Zongmian alone submitted repeated memorials on the matter.
translations.idiomatic: By then Li Quan's treasonous designs were already known, yet no one dared speak out—only Zongmian submitted memorial after memorial on the subject.

sentences.zh: 又言：「欲人謀之合，莫若通下情。

translations.literal: He also said: "If one wishes men's counsel to agree, nothing is better than opening channels to the feelings below.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "If you wish counsel to converge, there is no better way than to let the truth from below reach you.

sentences.zh: 人多好諂，揣所悅意則侈其言，度所惡聞則小其事。

translations.literal: Most people are fond of flattery: guessing what will please, they exaggerate; guessing what one hates to hear, they belittle the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Most men love to flatter: they inflate their words when they guess what will please you, and diminish the matter when they guess what you do not wish to hear.

sentences.zh: 上既壅塞，下亦欺誣，則成敗得失之機、理亂安危之故，將孰從而上聞哉？

translations.literal: When above is blocked and below also deceives, then by what means will the turning points of success and failure and the causes of order, chaos, safety, and peril reach the throne?
translations.idiomatic: When the court is sealed off above and deception reigns below, how will the turning points of victory and defeat, or the roots of order and chaos, ever reach your ears?

sentences.zh: 不聞則不戒，待其事至乃駭而圖之，抑已晚矣。

translations.literal: What is not heard is not guarded against; to wait until the event arrives and only then be alarmed and take counsel is already too late.
translations.idiomatic: What you do not hear, you cannot guard against; to wait until disaster strikes and only then be alarmed into action is already far too late.

sentences.zh: 欲財計之豐，莫若節國用。

translations.literal: If one wishes the state accounts to be ample, nothing is better than economizing on state expenditure.
translations.idiomatic: If you wish the treasury to be full, there is no better way than to restrain state spending.

sentences.zh: 善爲國者常使財勝事，不使事勝財。

translations.literal: One who governs a state well always makes wealth exceed affairs, and does not let affairs exceed wealth.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler who governs well always keeps resources ahead of demands, never letting demands outrun resources.

sentences.zh: 今山東之旅，坐糜我金穀，湖南、江右、閩中之寇，蹂踐我州縣，苟浮費泛用，又從而侵耗之，則漏卮難盈，蠹木易壞。

translations.literal: Now the armies in Shandong sit idle consuming our gold and grain; bandits in Hunan, Jiangyou, and Minzhong trample our prefectures and counties—if wasteful spending and indiscriminate use further drain and waste, then a leaking vessel is hard to fill and worm-eaten timber easily rots.
translations.idiomatic: Today our armies in Shandong consume gold and grain to no purpose, while rebels in Hunan, Jiangyou, and Fujian ravage our prefectures and counties; if wasteful spending further drains what remains, the treasury will be like a leaking vessel that cannot be filled, or worm-eaten timber that cannot stand.

sentences.zh: 設有緩急，必將窘于調度，而事機失矣。

translations.literal: Should urgency arise, one will necessarily be straitened in provisioning, and the moment for action will be lost.
translations.idiomatic: When crisis comes, you will find yourself unable to mobilize resources in time, and the moment for decisive action will be lost.

sentences.zh: 欲邦本之固，莫若寬民力。

translations.literal: If one wishes the foundation of the state to be firm, nothing is better than easing the burden on the people.
translations.idiomatic: If you wish the foundations of the state to be secure, there is no better way than to lighten the burden on the people.

sentences.zh: 州縣之間，聚斂者多，椎剝之風，浸以成習。

translations.literal: Between prefectures and counties there are many who amass levies; the wind of extortion has gradually become custom.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the prefectures and counties, tax collectors multiply, and the habit of squeezing the people has become entrenched.

sentences.zh: 民生窮踧，怨憤莫伸，嘯聚山林，勢所必至。

translations.literal: The people's livelihood is driven to extremity; grievance and anger find no outlet—gathering in the hills and forests with a cry is the course events must take.
translations.idiomatic: When the people are driven to destitution and their grievances have no outlet, they will inevitably band together in the mountains and forests.

sentences.zh: 救焚拯溺，可不亟爲之謀哉？」

translations.literal: To rescue from fire and save from drowning—can one fail to plan for this urgently?"
translations.idiomatic: When the house is on fire and men are drowning, can you afford not to act at once?"

sentences.zh: 尋改兼侍右郎官。

translations.literal: Soon after he was transferred to concurrently serve as a bureau director in the Right Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly thereafter he was reassigned to concurrently serve as a bureau director in the Right Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 明年入對，言天災甚切。

translations.literal: The next year on audience he spoke with great urgency of heavenly calamities.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, at an imperial audience, he spoke with great urgency about natural disasters and their meaning.

sentences.zh: 四年，差知台州。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was assigned to know Taizhou Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was appointed prefect of Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，直秘閣、知婺州。

translations.literal: The next year he was made a direct academician of the Secret Pavilion and prefect of Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was made a direct academician of the Secret Pavilion and appointed prefect of Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 六年冬，召赴行在，未行。

translations.literal: In the winter of the sixth year he was summoned to the mobile court but had not yet departed.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the sixth year he was summoned to the mobile court but had not yet set out.

sentences.zh: 端平元年，進直寶章閣，依舊任。

translations.literal: In the first year of Duanping he was advanced to direct academician of the Baozhang Pavilion, retaining his former post.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Duanping (1234) he was promoted to direct academician of the Baozhang Pavilion while retaining his prefectural post.

sentences.zh: 越月，以宗正丞兼權右司召，改尚左郎官，兼職仍舊。

translations.literal: Within the month he was summoned as vice-director of the Directorate of the Imperial Clan with acting charge of the Right Secretariat; he was changed to bureau director in the Left Secretariat, his concurrent duties remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: Within the month he was recalled as vice-director of the Directorate of the Imperial Clan with acting charge of the Right Secretariat, then transferred to bureau director in the Left Secretariat while keeping his other duties.

sentences.zh: 尋兼左司。

translations.literal: Soon after he was given concurrent charge of the Left Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly thereafter he was given concurrent charge of the Left Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 五月，面對，言四事：「守公道以悅人心，行實政以興治功，謹命令以一觀聽，明賞罰以示勸懲。」

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on a face-to-face audience, he spoke of four matters: "Uphold impartial justice to please people's hearts, carry out real administration to raise the achievements of governance, be strict in commands to unify what is seen and heard, and make rewards and punishments clear to show encouragement and restraint."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, at a face-to-face audience, he set forth four principles: "Uphold impartial justice to win the people's hearts; carry out genuine policies to advance good governance; enforce your commands strictly so that all may see and hear alike; and make rewards and punishments clear to encourage the worthy and restrain the wicked."

sentences.zh: 次言楮幣：「願詔有司，始自乘輿宮掖，下至百司庶府，核其冗蠹者節之，歲省十萬，則十萬之楮可捐，歲省百萬，則百萬之楮可捐也。

translations.literal: He next spoke of paper currency: "I wish Your Majesty would decree that the responsible offices, beginning with the imperial carriage and palace quarters and extending down to the hundred bureaus and common offices, examine and cut redundant waste; if a hundred thousand is saved in a year, then a hundred thousand in notes may be withdrawn; if a million is saved, then a million in notes may be withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: He then turned to paper currency: "I urge Your Majesty to decree that responsible offices, from the imperial household and palace down to every bureau and office, identify and eliminate waste; save a hundred thousand taels in a year, and a hundred thousand in notes may be withdrawn; save a million, and a million in notes may be withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 行之既久，捐之益多，錢楮相當，所至流轉，則操吾贏縮之柄不在楮矣。」

translations.literal: Carried out over time, withdrawals will grow ever greater; when coin and notes are equivalent and circulate wherever they go, then the handle of our surplus and deficit will no longer lie in the notes alone."
translations.idiomatic: Pursued over time, withdrawals will grow; when coin and notes stand in proper balance and circulate freely, the power to expand or contract the money supply will no longer rest on paper alone."

sentences.zh: 拜監察御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 時方謀出師汴、洛，宗勉言：「今朝廷安恬，無異于常時。

translations.literal: At the time they were planning to send troops to Bian and Luoyang; Zongmian said: "Now the court is at ease and untroubled, no different from ordinary times.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the court was planning a campaign toward Bian and Luoyang; Zongmian said: "The court today sits in complacent ease, no different from ordinary times.

sentences.zh: 士卒未精銳，資糧未充衍，器械未犀利，城壁未繕修。

translations.literal: The soldiers are not yet elite and sharp; provisions are not yet full and abundant; weapons are not yet keen; walls are not yet repaired.
translations.idiomatic: The troops are not yet trained and sharp; supplies are not yet ample; weapons are not yet ready; fortifications are not yet repaired.

sentences.zh: 于斯時也，守禦猶不可，而欲進取可乎？

translations.literal: At such a time, even defense is not yet possible—how can one desire to advance and seize?
translations.idiomatic: At such a moment, even defense is doubtful—how can we speak of going on the offensive?

sentences.zh: 借曰今日得蔡，明日得海，又明日得宿、毫，然得之者未必可守。

translations.literal: Grant that today we take Cai, tomorrow Haizhou, the day after Suzhou and Bozhou—yet what is taken may not necessarily be held.
translations.idiomatic: Suppose we take Cai today, Haizhou tomorrow, Suzhou and Bozhou the day after—even then, what we seize we may not be able to hold.

sentences.zh: 萬一含怒蓄忿，變生倉猝，將何以濟？

translations.literal: If by chance the enemy nurses anger and stored resentment and change arises in haste, with what will we cope?
translations.idiomatic: If the enemy, nursing anger, strikes back in sudden fury, how will we answer?

sentences.zh: 臣之所陳，豈曰外患之終不可平、土宇終不可復哉？

translations.literal: What your servant has presented—does it mean that external troubles can never be pacified or territory never recovered?
translations.idiomatic: What I have said—is it that foreign enemies can never be subdued or our lost lands never recovered?

sentences.zh: 亦欲量力以有爲、相時而後動耳。

translations.literal: It is only that one should act within one's strength and move only after gauging the time.
translations.idiomatic: I mean only that we should act within our strength and move only when the time is right.

sentences.zh: 願詔大臣，愛日力以修內治，合人謀以嚴邊防，節冗費以裕邦財，招強勇以壯國勢。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty would decree to the great ministers to cherish days and strength to repair internal governance, unite men's counsel to tighten frontier defense, cut redundant expenses to enrich state finances, and recruit the strong and brave to bolster national power.
translations.idiomatic: I urge Your Majesty to command the chief ministers to devote every day to internal reform, unite counsel to strengthen the borders, cut wasteful spending to enrich the treasury, and recruit the strong and brave to build national strength.

sentences.zh: 仍飭沿邊將帥，毋好虛名而受實害，左控右扼，毋失機先。

translations.literal: Further instruct the frontier generals not to love empty reputation while suffering real harm, to control left and choke right, and not to lose the initiative.
translations.idiomatic: Further instruct frontier commanders not to chase empty glory at the cost of real harm, to hold the line on every flank, and never to lose the initiative.

sentences.zh: 則以逸待勞，以主御客，庶可保其無虞。

translations.literal: Then, resting while the enemy labors, host facing guest, one may perhaps keep things free of worry.
translations.idiomatic: Then, resting while the enemy toils, defending as the host against the invader, we may hope to remain secure.

sentences.zh: 若使本根壯固，士馬精強，觀釁而動，用兵未晚。」

translations.literal: If the root is made firm and soldiers and horses are elite and strong, watching for an opening before moving—then to use arms is not too late."
translations.idiomatic: When our foundations are solid and our armies strong, we may watch for an opening and strike—it will not then be too late for war."

sentences.zh: 已而洛師潰，又言：「昔之所慮者在當守而冒進，今之所慮者在欲守而不能。

translations.literal: Before long the Luoyang army collapsed; he spoke again: "What we once feared was that we should defend yet rashly advance; what we now fear is that we wish to defend yet cannot.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after the Luoyang army collapsed, he spoke again: "What we once feared was advancing when we should have held fast; what we now fear is wanting to hold and being unable to.

sentences.zh: 何地可控扼，何兵可調遣，何將可捍禦，何糧可給餉，皆當預作措畫。」

translations.literal: What places can be held and choked, what troops can be deployed, what generals can defend, what grain can supply rations—all must be planned in advance."
translations.idiomatic: Which positions can be held, which troops deployed, which generals assigned to defense, which grain used for supply—all must be planned in advance."

sentences.zh: 又言內降之敝，大略謂：「王府後宅之宮僚，戚裏奄寺之恩賞，綸綍直下，不經都省，竿牘陳請，時出禁廷，此皆大臣所當執奏。

translations.literal: He also spoke of the abuses of inner decrees, saying in summary: "Palace staff of the princely mansions and inner quarters, favor-grants to consort kin and eunuchs—the sealed edict descends straight down without passing the chief secretariat; petitions are submitted and sometimes issue from the forbidden court—these are all matters the great ministers ought to remonstrate upon.
translations.idiomatic: He also addressed the abuse of imperial rescripts issued from within the palace, saying in essence: "Favors for palace staff, consort kin, and eunuchs—edicts that bypass the chief secretariat, petitions that issue from the inner court—these are matters on which chief ministers ought to remonstrate.

sentences.zh: 夫先事而言，見幾而諫，不可謂之專。

translations.literal: To speak before the event, to remonstrate upon seeing the first sign—this cannot be called overstepping.
translations.idiomatic: To speak before disaster strikes, to remonstrate at the first sign—this cannot be called overstepping one's authority.

sentences.zh: 善則行之，否則止之，不可謂之專。

translations.literal: If good, carry it out; if not, stop it—this cannot be called overstepping.
translations.idiomatic: To approve what is right and halt what is wrong—this cannot be called overstepping.

sentences.zh: 命出君上，政歸中書，不可謂之專。

translations.literal: When commands issue from the ruler above and administration returns to the Secretariat, this cannot be called overstepping.
translations.idiomatic: When orders come from the throne and policy rests with the Secretariat—this cannot be called overstepping.

sentences.zh: 苟以專權爲嫌，不以救過爲急，每事希旨迎合，迨其命令已下，闕失已彰，然後言事之人從而論列之，其累聖德亦多矣。

translations.literal: If one takes usurpation of authority as the worry and does not take remedying faults as urgent, on every matter currying favor and compliance—then when the command has already been issued and the lapse already manifest, only then do those who speak on affairs follow with their critiques; the burden on sagely virtue is also great.
translations.idiomatic: If ministers fear being called overbearing more than they fear failing to correct error, and on every matter curry favor—then when the edict has already gone forth and the harm is already done, critics follow only to catalogue the damage; how much greater the stain on Your Majesty's virtue.

sentences.zh: 況言之未必聽，聽之未必行乎？」

translations.literal: Moreover, what is said is not necessarily heard, and what is heard is not necessarily carried out?"
translations.idiomatic: And even then, what is said is not necessarily heard, and what is heard is not necessarily done?"

sentences.zh: 進左司諫。

translations.literal: He was promoted to remonstrance officer of the Left Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to remonstrance officer of the Left Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 明年春，兼侍講。

translations.literal: In the spring of the next year he was given concurrent appointment as lecturer-in-waiting.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the following year he was concurrently appointed lecturer-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 首言：「均、房、安、蘄、光、化等處兵禍甚烈，然江面可藉以無憂者，猶有襄州，今又告變矣。

translations.literal: He first spoke: "Jun, Fang, An, Qi, Guang, and Hua and other places suffer military calamity most fiercely; yet on the river line what could be relied on for freedom from worry was still Xiangzhou—now it too reports rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke first: "Military disaster rages at Jun, Fang, An, Qi, Guang, and Hua; yet on the Yangzi what still gave us hope was Xiangzhou—and now Xiangzhou too reports rebellion.

sentences.zh: 襄州失則江陵危，江陵危則長江之險不足恃。

translations.literal: If Xiangzhou is lost, then Jiangling is endangered; if Jiangling is endangered, then the Yangzi's strategic depth cannot be relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: If Xiangzhou falls, Jiangling is in peril; if Jiangling falls, the Yangzi's defenses cannot be trusted.

sentences.zh: 昔之所慮猶在秋，今之所慮者祗在旦夕。

translations.literal: What we once feared was still months away; what we now fear is only a matter of morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: What we once feared was still months away; what we fear now may come at any hour.

sentences.zh: 江陵或不守，則事迫勢蹙，必有存亡之憂，悔將何及？」

translations.literal: If Jiangling perhaps cannot be held, then affairs press and the situation tightens—there will necessarily be worry over survival and extinction; what regret will avail?"
translations.idiomatic: If Jiangling cannot be held, the crisis will close in and the dynasty itself will hang in the balance—what use will regret be then?"

sentences.zh: 拜殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed palace attendant censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed palace attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 時淮西制置使兼沿江制置副使史嵩之兼知鄂州，就鄂建牙。

translations.literal: At the time the Huai West commissioner and vice commissioner along the river, Shi Songzhi, was concurrently prefect of Ezhou and established his headquarters at E.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Shi Songzhi, Huai West commissioner and vice commissioner along the Yangzi, was concurrently prefect of Ezhou and had established his headquarters there.

sentences.zh: 宗勉言：「荊、襄殘破，淮西正當南北之交，嵩之當置司淮西，則脈絡相連，可以應援，邈在鄂渚，豈無鞭不及腹之慮。

translations.literal: Zongmian said: "Jing and Xiang are ravaged and broken; Huai West lies right at the junction of north and south—Songzhi ought to place his headquarters in Huai West, so that the arteries connect and he can respond in support; stationed far at Ezhou, is there not worry that the whip cannot reach the belly?
translations.idiomatic: Zongmian said: "Jing and Xiang lie in ruins; Huai West sits at the junction of north and south. Songzhi ought to establish his headquarters in Huai West, where the lines of communication connect and he can respond in support. Posted far away at Ezhou, he risks being unable to reach where he is needed.

sentences.zh: 若云防江爲急，欲藉嵩之于鄂渚經理，然齊安正與武昌對，如就彼措置防扼，則藩籬壯而江面安矣。

translations.literal: If one says defending the river is urgent and wishes to rely on Songzhi at Ezhou to manage affairs—yet Qi'an lies directly opposite Wuchang; if arrangements for defense are made there, then the barrier will be strong and the river line secure.
translations.idiomatic: If the urgent need is river defense and you wish Songzhi to manage affairs from Ezhou, consider that Qi'an lies directly opposite Wuchang; station him there to organize the defense, and the barrier will be strong and the river secure.

sentences.zh: 所謂欲保江南先守江北也。

translations.literal: This is what is meant by: to preserve Jiangnan, first hold Jiangbei.
translations.idiomatic: This is the principle: to save the south, first hold the north bank.

sentences.zh: 當別擇鄂守，徑令嵩之移司齊安。」

translations.literal: Another should be chosen as prefect of E, and Songzhi should be ordered directly to move his headquarters to Qi'an."
translations.idiomatic: Choose another man as prefect of E, and order Songzhi to move his headquarters directly to Qi'an.

sentences.zh: 詔侍從、兩省、台諫條陳邊事，宗勉率合台奏：「蜀之四路，已失其二，成都隔絕，莫知存亡。

translations.literal: An edict ordered attendants-in-waiting, the two secretariats, and the censorate and remonstrance bureaus to set forth border affairs item by item; Zongmian led the united censorate in memorializing: "Of Sichuan's four circuits, two are already lost; Chengdu is cut off and none knows whether it survives.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered court officials, the two secretariats, and the censorate to submit plans on border affairs; Zongmian led the united censorate in memorializing: "Of Sichuan's four circuits, two are lost; Chengdu is cut off and none knows whether it still stands.

sentences.zh: 諸司退保夔門，未必能守。

translations.literal: The various offices have fallen back to defend Kuimen, yet may not necessarily be able to hold.
translations.idiomatic: The offices have fallen back to defend Kuimen, yet may not be able to hold even that.

sentences.zh: 襄漢昨失九郡，今郢破，荊門又破，江陵孤城，何以能立？

translations.literal: Xiang and Han yesterday lost nine prefectures; now Ying is taken, Jingmen also taken—how can Jiangling, a lone city, stand?
translations.idiomatic: Xiang and Han have lost nine prefectures; Ying has fallen, Jingmen has fallen—how can Jiangling, a lone city, endure?

sentences.zh: 兩淮之地，人民奔迸，井邑丘墟，嗚呼危哉！

translations.literal: In the two Huai regions the people flee in panic; towns and hamlets are ruins—alas, how perilous!
translations.idiomatic: Across the two Huai regions the people flee in terror; towns lie in ruins—alas, how desperate our plight!

sentences.zh: 陛下誠能亟下哀痛之詔，以身率先，深自貶損，服御飲宴，一從簡儉，放後宮浮食之女，罷掖庭不急之費，止錫齎，絕工役，出內帑儲蓄以風動四方。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty can urgently issue a decree of grief and pain, taking the lead in person, deeply abasing yourself, making dress, equipage, food, and banquets all follow simplicity, releasing superfluous women of the inner palace, abolishing non-urgent expenses of the palace women quarters, stopping bestowals, cutting off labor corvée, and bringing out inner-treasury reserves to stir the four quarters by example—
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty will urgently issue a decree of mourning and repentance, take the lead in person, humble yourself deeply, simplify dress and banquets, release superfluous palace women, cut nonessential expenses of the inner quarters, halt lavish grants, stop wasteful projects, and draw on the inner treasury to set an example for the realm.

sentences.zh: 然後勸諭戚畹、世臣，隨力輸財，以佐公家之調度。

translations.literal: then exhort consort kin and hereditary ministers to contribute wealth according to their means to assist the state's provisioning.
translations.idiomatic: Then urge consort kin and hereditary ministers to contribute according to their means to aid the state's finances.

sentences.zh: 分上流淮西、淮東爲三帥，而以江淮大帥總之。

translations.literal: Divide the upper reaches, Huai West, and Huai East into three commanders, with a great commander of Jiang and Huai overseeing them.
translations.idiomatic: Divide the upper Yangzi, Huai West, and Huai East among three commanders, under a supreme commander for the Jiang-Huai region.

sentences.zh: 或因今任，或擇長才，分地而守，聽令而行。

translations.literal: Either retain present appointees or select men of outstanding talent, each guarding his territory and obeying orders in action.
translations.idiomatic: Retain present commanders or choose men of talent, assign each his territory, and let them act on unified orders.

sentences.zh: 以公私之財分給四處，俾之招潰卒，募流民之強壯者，以充遊兵，以補軍籍。

translations.literal: Distribute public and private wealth to the four sectors, enabling them to recruit scattered troops and enlist strong men among displaced people as roaming soldiers to fill the military registers.
translations.idiomatic: Distribute public and private funds to the four sectors, so they may gather scattered troops and enlist strong men among refugees as mobile forces to fill the rolls.

sentences.zh: 仍選沿流諸郡將士爲捍禦之圖，猶可支吾。

translations.literal: Further select generals and soldiers of the prefectures along the river to draw up plans of defense—one may still hold on.
translations.idiomatic: Further select commanders along the river to organize the defense—we may still hold the line.

sentences.zh: 不然將水陸俱下，大合荊楚之衆，擾我上流，江以南震盪矣。

translations.literal: Otherwise they will come down by water and land together, mass the hosts of Jing and Chu, harass our upper reaches, and the lands south of the Yangzi will be shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise the enemy will advance by land and water, mass the armies of Jing and Chu, strike our upper Yangzi, and the lands south of the river will be shaken to their foundations.

sentences.zh: 或謂其勢強盛，宜於講和，欲出金繒以奉之，是抱薪救火，空國與敵矣。」

translations.literal: Some say their power is strong and one ought to seek peace, wishing to offer gold and silks to serve them—this is carrying firewood to put out a fire, emptying the state for the enemy."
translations.idiomatic: Some say their power is too great and we should sue for peace, offering gold and silk to appease them—this is carrying firewood to fight a fire, hollowing out the state for the enemy."

sentences.zh: 進工部侍郎兼給事中，仍侍講。

translations.literal: He was advanced to vice minister of Works with concurrent appointment as supervising secretary, still lecturer-in-waiting.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice minister of Works with concurrent appointment as supervising secretary, retaining his post as lecturer-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 復上疏言：「陛下憂勤于路朝之頃，而入爲宴安所移，切劘於廣廈之間，而退爲便佞所惑。

translations.literal: He again submitted a memorial saying: "Your Majesty was diligent in care on the road and at court, yet on entering was shifted by ease and pleasure; you were earnest in the broad halls, yet on retiring were deluded by the facile and fawning.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted another memorial: "Your Majesty was diligent in care on the road and at court, yet once within the palace you succumbed to ease; you were earnest in the great halls, yet in private you were swayed by flatterers.

sentences.zh: 不聞減退宮女，而嬪嬙已溢于昔時；

translations.literal: We have not heard of reducing palace women, yet consorts and attendants already exceed former times;
translations.idiomatic: We hear no word of reducing palace women, yet consorts and attendants already exceed former times;

sentences.zh: 不聞褒錄功臣，而節鉞先加于外戚；

translations.literal: we have not heard of rewarding meritorious ministers, yet command seals were first bestowed on consort kin;
translations.idiomatic: we hear no word of rewarding meritorious ministers, yet military commands were first given to consort kin;

sentences.zh: 不聞出內貯以犒戰士，而金帛多靡于浮費。

translations.literal: we have not heard of bringing out inner stores to reward fighting soldiers, yet gold and silks are mostly wasted on frivolous expenditure.
translations.idiomatic: we hear no word of drawing on the inner treasury to reward soldiers, yet gold and silk are squandered on frivolous spending.

sentences.zh: 陛下之舉動，人心所視以爲卷舒者也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's conduct is what men's hearts watch to know whether things tighten or ease.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's every act is what the people watch to know whether times will tighten or ease.

sentences.zh: 陛下既不以爲憂，則誰復爲陛下憂。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty does not take it as worry, then who again will worry for Your Majesty?"
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty does not worry, who will worry for you?"

sentences.zh: 擢諫議大夫兼侍讀。

translations.literal: He was elevated to remonstrance and policy adviser with concurrent appointment as reader-in-waiting.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to remonstrance and policy adviser with concurrent appointment as reader-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 首言邊事當增兵防托上流。

translations.literal: He first spoke that on border affairs troops should be increased to defend and hold the upper reaches.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke first that border affairs required more troops to defend the upper Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 又言：「求諫非難而受諫爲難，受諫非難而從諫爲難。

translations.literal: He also said: "Seeking remonstrance is not hard, but receiving remonstrance is hard; receiving remonstrance is not hard, but following remonstrance is hard.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "It is not hard to invite remonstrance, but hard to accept it; not hard to accept it, but hard to follow it.

sentences.zh: 苟聞之不以爲戒，玩之不以爲信，卒使危言鯁論，無益於世用，無救于時危，其與拒諫者相去一間耳。」

translations.literal: If what is heard is not taken as warning, and what is toyed with is not taken as trust, in the end stern words and lodged arguments are of no use to the world and save nothing from the peril of the times—the distance from those who reject remonstrance is but a narrow space."
translations.idiomatic: If what you hear does not alarm you, and what you toy with you do not trust, then even the sternest counsel will serve no purpose and save us from nothing—the distance between you and those who reject remonstrance is but a hair's breadth."

sentences.zh: 進端明殿學士、同簽書樞密院事。

translations.literal: He was advanced to academician of the Duanming Hall and associate signer of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to academician of the Duanming Hall and associate signer of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 未幾，進簽書。

translations.literal: Before long he was advanced to signer.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to full signer.

sentences.zh: 時王楫復求歲幣銀絹各二十萬，宗勉言：「輕諾者多後患，當守元約可也。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Qi again sought annual tribute of two hundred thousand taels of silver and bolts of silk each; Zongmian said: "Those who lightly promise often have many later troubles—one should keep to the original treaty.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Wang Qi again demanded annual tribute of two hundred thousand taels of silver and bolts of silk each; Zongmian said: "Light promises breed heavy troubles—we should hold to the original treaty.

sentences.zh: 然比之開禧時，物價騰踴奚啻倍蓰矣。」

translations.literal: Yet compared with the Kaixi period, prices have soared—how much more than doubled and redoubled."
translations.idiomatic: Yet compared with the Kaixi period, prices have more than doubled and redoubled."

sentences.zh: 史嵩之開督府，力主和議，宗勉言：「使者可疑者三。

translations.literal: Shi Songzhi opened a supervisory headquarters and strongly advocated peace talks; Zongmian said: "The envoy gives three grounds for suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Songzhi opened a supervisory headquarters and strongly advocated peace; Zongmian said: "The envoy gives three grounds for suspicion.

sentences.zh: 嵩之職在督戰，如收復襄、光，控扼施、澧，招集山砦，保固江流，皆今所當爲。

translations.literal: Songzhi's duty is to supervise warfare—such as recovering Xiang and Guang, controlling Shi and Li, gathering mountain stockades, and securing the river line—all are what should be done now.
translations.idiomatic: Songzhi's duty is to supervise warfare—recovering Xiang and Guang, holding Shi and Li, gathering mountain stockades, securing the river line—all this is what he should be doing now.

sentences.zh: 若所主在和，則凡有機會可乘，不無退縮之意，必至虛捐歲月，坐失事功。」

translations.literal: If what he advocates is peace, then whenever there is an opening to exploit there will be no lack of intent to shrink back, and months will be wasted in vain until achievements are lost by sitting idle."
translations.idiomatic: If his heart is set on peace, then whenever an opportunity arises he will shrink back, wasting months until every chance for achievement is lost."

sentences.zh: 進參知政事。

translations.literal: He was advanced to participant in governance.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 及拜左丞相兼樞密使，守法度，抑僥倖，不私親黨，召用老成，尤樂聞讜言。

translations.literal: When he was appointed left grand councilor with concurrent charge as commissioner of military affairs, he upheld law and measure, checked favoritism, did not favor kin and faction, summoned the mature and experienced, and especially delighted in hearing forthright speech.
translations.idiomatic: When he was appointed left grand councilor and commissioner of military affairs, he upheld the law, checked favoritism, showed no partiality to kin or faction, promoted seasoned men, and especially welcomed forthright counsel.

sentences.zh: 趙汝騰嘗以宗勉爲公清之相。

translations.literal: Zhao Ruteng once regarded Zongmian as a minister of public integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ruteng once called Zongmian a minister of public integrity.

sentences.zh: 以光祿大夫、觀文殿大學士致仕，卒，贈少師，諡文清。

translations.literal: He retired as Grandee of Splendid Happiness and academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature, died, and was posthumously made Junior Mentor with the posthumous title Wénqīng.
translations.idiomatic: He retired as Grandee of Splendid Happiness and academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature, died, and was posthumously made Junior Mentor with the posthumous title Wénqīng.

sentences.zh: 袁甫，字廣微，寶文閣直學士燮之子。

translations.literal: Yuan Fu, style name Guangwei, was the son of Yuan Xie, direct academician of the Baowen Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Fu, courtesy name Guangwei, was the son of Yuan Xie, direct academician of the Baowen Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 嘉定七年進士第一。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Jiading he placed first in the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Jiading he placed first in the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 簽書建康軍節度判官廳公事，授秘書省正字。

translations.literal: He signed documents as secretary of the Jianning Military Commission judicial office and was appointed rectifier in the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: He signed documents as secretary of the Jianning Military Commission judicial office and was appointed rectifier in the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 入對，論「君天下不可一日無懼心。

translations.literal: On audience he discussed that "one who rules the realm must not go a single day without a heart of dread.
translations.idiomatic: On audience he said that "a ruler must never go a single day without a heart of dread.

sentences.zh: 今之可懼者，大端有五：端良者斥，諂諛者用，杜忠臣敢諫之門，可懼也；

translations.literal: What is to be dreaded today has five great heads: the upright are dismissed and flatterers employed, the gate for loyal ministers to remonstrate boldly is shut—this is to be dreaded;
translations.idiomatic: What must be dreaded today has five great heads: the upright are dismissed and flatterers employed, the gate for loyal remonstrance is shut—this is to be dreaded;

sentences.zh: 兵戈既興，饋餉不繼，根本一虛，則有蕭牆之憂，可懼也；

translations.literal: war having begun, rations not continuing, the root once hollowed then there is worry within the palace walls—this is to be dreaded;
translations.idiomatic: war has begun, supplies do not keep pace, the root is hollowed and trouble within the walls follows—this is to be dreaded;

sentences.zh: 陛下深居高拱，群臣奉行簿書，獨運密謀之意勝，而虛心咨訪之意微，天下迫切之情無由上聞，可懼也；

translations.literal: Your Majesty sits deep and high with arms folded, the ministers carry out ledgers, the intent to operate secret plans alone prevails while the intent to consult with an open heart is slight, the realm's urgent feelings cannot reach above—this is to be dreaded;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty sits aloof while ministers shuffle papers, secret plotting prevails and open consultation fades, the people's urgent needs cannot reach you—this is to be dreaded;

sentences.zh: 外患未弭，內患方深，而熙熙然無異平時，自謂雅量足以鎮浮，不知宴安實爲鴆毒，可懼也；

translations.literal: external troubles not yet quelled, internal troubles deepening, yet all is gay as in normal times, thinking one's magnanimity enough to calm unrest, not knowing ease and pleasure are in truth poison—this is to be dreaded;
translations.idiomatic: foreign threats are not yet ended, internal troubles deepen, yet the court is gay as in peacetime, trusting magnanimity to calm unrest, not knowing that ease is poison—this is to be dreaded;

sentences.zh: 陛下恭儉有餘，剛斷不足，庸夫憸人，苟求富貴，而未聞大明黜陟，軍帥交結，州郡賄賂，皆自貴近化之，可懼也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is respectful and frugal in surplus yet insufficient in firm resolve; mediocre men and the crafty seek wealth and rank, yet one does not hear of great clear promotions and demotions; military commanders form factions and prefectures give bribes—all are transformed from those near and dear—this is to be dreaded.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is respectful and frugal yet lacks firm resolve; mediocre and crafty men seek wealth and rank, yet we hear no clear promotions and demotions; generals form factions and prefectures give bribes—all learned from those close to the throne—this is to be dreaded.

sentences.zh: 其他禍幾亂萌，不可悉數，將何以答天譴、召和氣哉？」

translations.literal: Other omens of disorder and sprouting evils cannot all be numbered—how will you answer heaven's reproof and summon harmony?"
translations.idiomatic: Other omens of disorder cannot all be counted—how will you answer heaven's reproof and summon harmony?"

sentences.zh: 次乞嚴守帥之選，並大軍之權，興屯田之利。

translations.literal: He next begged strict selection of commanders and consolidation of great-army authority, and the profit of military colonies.
translations.idiomatic: He next urged strict selection of commanders, consolidation of army authority, and the benefits of military colonies.

sentences.zh: 遷校書郎，轉對，言「邊事之病，不在外而在內。

translations.literal: He was transferred to collator, and on rotated audience said: "The sickness of border affairs lies not outside but within.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to collator, and on rotated audience said: "The sickness of border affairs lies not outside but within.

sentences.zh: 偷安之根不去，規摹終不立；

translations.literal: If the root of stealing ease is not removed, the plan will never be established;
translations.idiomatic: If the root of complacency is not removed, no plan will ever stand;

sentences.zh: 壅蔽之根不去，血脈終不通；

translations.literal: if the root of obstruction is not removed, the arteries will never connect;
translations.idiomatic: if the root of obstruction is not removed, the arteries of communication will never open;

sentences.zh: 忌嫉之根不去，將帥終不可擇；

translations.literal: if the root of jealousy is not removed, generals can never finally be chosen;
translations.idiomatic: if the root of jealousy is not removed, worthy generals can never be chosen;

sentences.zh: 欺誕之根不去，兵財終不可治。

translations.literal: if the root of deception is not removed, troops and finances can never finally be governed.
translations.idiomatic: if the root of deception is not removed, troops and finances can never be governed.

sentences.zh: 祖宗之御天下，政事雖委中書，然必擇風采著聞者爲台諫，敢於論駁者爲給、舍，所以戢官邪、肅朝綱也。

translations.literal: When the ancestors ruled the realm, though administration was entrusted to the Secretariat, they always chose men of distinguished bearing for the censorate and remonstrance, and men who dared debate for the supervising secretaries and remonstrators—thus to restrain official wickedness and tighten court discipline.
translations.idiomatic: When the ancestors ruled, though administration rested with the Secretariat, they always chose men of distinguished bearing for the censorate and remonstrance, and men who dared debate for the supervising secretaries—thus to restrain corruption and tighten court discipline.

sentences.zh: 今日誠體是意以行之，豈復有偷安壅蔽者哉？」

translations.literal: If today one truly embodies this intent in practice, how could there still be those who steal ease and obstruct?"
translations.idiomatic: If today you truly embody this intent, how could complacency and obstruction survive?"

sentences.zh: 出通判湖州，考常平敝原以增積貯，核隱產，增附嬰兒局。

translations.literal: He went out as vice-prefect of Huzhou, examined the abuses of the Ever-Normal Granary to increase reserves, verified hidden property, and expanded the Infant Relief Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as vice-prefect of Huzhou, reformed Ever-Normal Granary abuses to increase reserves, verified hidden property, and expanded the Infant Relief Bureau.

sentences.zh: 遷秘書郎，尋遷著作佐郎、知徽州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to secretary, and soon to assistant compiler and prefect of Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to secretary, and soon to assistant compiler and prefect of Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 治先教化，崇學校，訪便民事上之：請蠲減婺源綢絹萬七千餘匹，茶租折帛錢萬五千餘貫，月樁錢六千餘貫；

translations.literal: He governed by education first, honored schools, and submitted convenient measures for the people: requesting exemption of more than seventeen thousand bolts of Wuyuan silk tribute, more than fifteen thousand strings of tea rent converted to cloth money, and more than six thousand strings of monthly quota money;
translations.idiomatic: He put education first, honored schools, and submitted measures for the people: requesting exemption of more than seventeen thousand bolts of Wuyuan silk tribute, more than fifteen thousand strings of tea rent in cloth money, and more than six thousand strings of monthly quota money;

sentences.zh: 請照咸平、紹興、乾道寬恤指揮，受納徽絹定每匹十兩；

translations.literal: requesting that according to the lenient relief directives of Xianping, Shaoxing, and Qiandao, Huizhou silk accepted in payment be fixed at ten taels per bolt;
translations.idiomatic: requesting that under the lenient relief directives of Xianping, Shaoxing, and Qiandao, Huizhou silk accepted in payment be fixed at ten taels per bolt;

sentences.zh: 請下轉運、常平兩司，豫蓄常平義倉備荒，興修陂塘，創築百梁。

translations.literal: requesting that the transport and Ever-Normal commissions store grain in advance against famine, repair dikes and ponds, and build the Hundred Bridges.
translations.idiomatic: requesting that the transport and Ever-Normal commissions store grain against famine, repair dikes and ponds, and build the Hundred Bridges.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，服除，知衢州。

translations.literal: He mourned his father; when the mourning ended he was made prefect of Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He mourned his father; when mourning ended he was made prefect of Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 立旬講，務以理義淑士心，歲撥助養士千緡。

translations.literal: He established decanal lectures, striving with principle and righteousness to refine scholars' hearts, and each year allocated a thousand strings to assist in supporting students.
translations.idiomatic: He established decanal lectures, striving with principle and righteousness to refine scholars' hearts, and each year allocated a thousand strings to support students.

sentences.zh: 西安、龍遊、常山三邑積窘預借，爲代輸三萬五千緡，蠲放四萬七千緡。

translations.literal: The three districts of Xi'an, Longyou, and Changshan had long suffered from advance requisitions; he paid thirty-five thousand strings on their behalf and remitted forty-seven thousand strings.
translations.idiomatic: The three districts of Xi'an, Longyou, and Changshan had long suffered advance requisitions; he paid thirty-five thousand strings on their behalf and remitted forty-seven thousand strings.

sentences.zh: 郡有義莊，買良田二百畝益之。

translations.literal: The prefecture had a charity estate; he bought two hundred mu of fertile fields to augment it.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture had a charity estate; he bought two hundred mu of fertile fields to augment it.

sentences.zh: 移提舉江東常平。

translations.literal: He was transferred to intendant of the Jiangdong Ever-Normal Granary.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to intendant of the Jiangdong Ever-Normal Granary.

sentences.zh: 適歲旱，亟發庫庾之積，凡州縣窠名隸倉司者，無新舊皆住催，爲錢六萬一千緡，米十有三萬七千、麥五千八百石，遣官分行振濟，饑者予粟，病者予藥，尺籍之單弱者，市民之失業者，皆曲軫之。

translations.literal: It happened to be a drought year; he urgently released accumulated stores. Of all items under the granary commission in prefectures and counties, whether old or new, collection was halted, amounting to sixty-one thousand strings in cash, one hundred thirty-seven thousand piculs of rice, and five thousand eight hundred shi of wheat; he sent officials to distribute relief by circuit—giving grain to the hungry, medicine to the sick, and showing care to those on the registers who were weak and to townspeople who had lost their livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: In a drought year he urgently released accumulated stores. For all items under the granary commission in prefectures and counties, whether old or new, he halted collection—sixty-one thousand strings in cash, one hundred thirty-seven thousand piculs of rice, and five thousand eight hundred shi of wheat—and sent officials to distribute relief: grain to the hungry, medicine to the sick, care to the weak on the registers, and to townspeople who had lost their livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 又告於朝曰：「江東或水而旱，或旱而水，重以雨雪連月，道殣相望，至有舉家枕藉而死者。

translations.literal: He also reported to the court: "In Jiangdong there is sometimes flood then drought, or drought then flood; added to months of continuous rain and snow, corpses line the roads, and there are even cases of whole families lying dead together.
translations.idiomatic: He also reported to the court: "In Jiangdong there is sometimes flood then drought, or drought then flood; with months of rain and snow, corpses line the roads, and whole families lie dead together.

sentences.zh: 此去麥熟尚賒，事勢益急。」

translations.literal: The wheat harvest is still far off and the situation grows more urgent."
translations.idiomatic: The wheat harvest is still far off and the situation grows more urgent."

sentences.zh: 詔給度牒百道助費。

translations.literal: An edict granted a hundred ordination certificates to help cover expenses.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted a hundred ordination certificates to help cover expenses.

sentences.zh: 時江、閩寇迫饒、信，慮民情易動，分榜諭安之。

translations.literal: At the time bandits from Jiang and Min pressed on Rao and Xin; fearing the people's hearts might be easily stirred, he posted proclamations to reassure them.
translations.idiomatic: At the time bandits from Jiang and Min pressed on Rao and Xin; fearing unrest among the people, he posted proclamations to reassure them.

sentences.zh: 檄諸郡，關制司，聞於朝，爲保境捍患之圖，寇迄不犯。

translations.literal: He dispatched orders to all prefectures and the frontier command, reported to the court, and drew up plans to protect the territory and repel harm—the bandits in the end did not invade.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched orders to all prefectures and the frontier command, reported to the court, and drew up plans to protect the territory—the bandits in the end did not invade.

sentences.zh: 遂提點本路刑獄兼提舉，移司番陽。

translations.literal: He was then made judicial intendant of the circuit with concurrent intendant duties, moving his headquarters to Poyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made judicial intendant of the circuit with concurrent intendant duties, moving his headquarters to Poyang.

sentences.zh: 霜殺桑，春夏雨久湖溢，諸郡被水，連請於朝，給度牒二百道賑恤之。

translations.literal: Frost killed the mulberry trees; spring and summer rains lasted long and lakes overflowed; many prefectures suffered flood; he repeatedly petitioned the court and was granted two hundred ordination certificates for relief.
translations.idiomatic: Frost killed the mulberry trees; spring and summer rains lasted long and lakes overflowed; many prefectures suffered flood; he repeatedly petitioned the court and was granted two hundred ordination certificates for relief.

sentences.zh: 盜起常山，調他州兵千人屯廣信以爲備。

translations.literal: Bandits rose in Changshan; he mobilized a thousand troops from another prefecture to garrison Guangxin as a precaution.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits rose in Changshan; he mobilized a thousand troops from another prefecture to garrison Guangxin as a precaution.

sentences.zh: 都城大火，上封事言：「上下不交，以言爲諱，天意人心，實同一機，災變之作，端由於此。

translations.literal: A great fire broke out in the capital; he submitted a sealed memorial saying: "Above and below do not communicate, speech is tabooed, the intent of heaven and the hearts of men are in truth one mechanism—the arising of disasters and portents stems from this.
translations.idiomatic: A great fire broke out in the capital; he submitted a sealed memorial saying: "Above and below do not communicate, speech is tabooed, heaven's intent and the people's hearts are one—the arising of disasters stems from this.

sentences.zh: 願下哀痛之詔，以回天意。」

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty would issue a decree of grief and pain to turn back heaven's intent."
translations.idiomatic: I wish Your Majesty would issue a decree of grief and pain to turn back heaven's intent."

sentences.zh: 詔求直言，復上疏言：「災起都邑，天意蓋欲陛下因其所可見，察其所不可見，行至公無私之心，全保護大臣之體，率屬群工，大明黜陟，與天下更始。」

translations.literal: An edict sought forthright speech; he again submitted a memorial saying: "The disaster arose in the capital; heaven's intent surely wishes Your Majesty, from what can be seen, to discern what cannot be seen, to carry impartiality without private ends to completion, fully to preserve the stature of protecting great ministers, to lead the host of officials in great clear promotions and demotions, and to make a fresh start with the realm."
translations.idiomatic: An edict sought forthright speech; he again submitted a memorial saying: "The disaster arose in the capital; heaven wishes Your Majesty, from what can be seen, to discern what cannot be seen, to act with impartiality, to protect the stature of great ministers, to lead officials in clear promotions and demotions, and to make a fresh start with the realm."

sentences.zh: 行部問民疾苦，薦循良，劾奸貪，決滯獄。

translations.literal: On tour he inquired into the people's hardships, recommended the upright and good, impeached the wicked and greedy, and decided stagnant cases.
translations.idiomatic: On tour he inquired into the people's hardships, recommended the upright, impeached the greedy, and decided stagnant cases.

sentences.zh: 所至詣學宮講說，創書院貴溪之南，祠先儒陸九淵。

translations.literal: Wherever he went he visited school halls to lecture, founded an academy south of Guixi, and enshrined the earlier Confucian Lu Jiuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he went he visited school halls to lecture, founded an academy south of Guixi, and enshrined the earlier Confucian Lu Jiuyuan.

sentences.zh: 歲大旱，請於朝，得度牒、緡錢、綾紙以助賑恤。

translations.literal: In a year of great drought he petitioned the court and obtained ordination certificates, strings of cash, and silk paper to aid relief.
translations.idiomatic: In a year of great drought he petitioned the court and obtained ordination certificates, strings of cash, and silk paper to aid relief.

sentences.zh: 疫癘大作，創藥院療之。

translations.literal: Epidemic illness broke out on a great scale; he founded a medicine hall to treat it.
translations.idiomatic: Epidemic illness broke out on a great scale; he founded a medicine hall to treat it.

sentences.zh: 前後持節江東五年，所活殆不可數計。

translations.literal: For five years in all he held credentials in Jiangdong; those he kept alive can hardly be counted.
translations.idiomatic: For five years in all he held credentials in Jiangdong; the lives he saved can hardly be counted.

sentences.zh: 轉將作監，領事如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to director of palace construction, retaining his former duties.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to director of palace construction, retaining his former duties.

sentences.zh: 繼力辭常平事。

translations.literal: He then strenuously declined Ever-Normal duties.
translations.idiomatic: He then strenuously declined Ever-Normal duties.

sentences.zh: 彗星見，詔求直言，上疏言：「皇天所以震怒者，由愁苦之民衆；

translations.literal: A comet appeared; an edict sought forthright speech; he submitted a memorial saying: "The reason the August Heaven is enraged is the multitude of the anguished and bitter;
translations.idiomatic: A comet appeared; an edict sought forthright speech; he submitted a memorial saying: "The reason heaven is enraged is the multitude of the anguished and bitter;

sentences.zh: 人民所以愁苦者，由貪冒之風熾。

translations.literal: the reason the people are anguished and bitter is that the wind of greed and usurpation burns hot.
translations.idiomatic: the reason the people are anguished and bitter is that the wind of greed and usurpation burns hot.

sentences.zh: 願一變上下交征之習，爲大公至正之歸。」

translations.literal: I wish to change at once the custom of mutual exaction above and below, and return to great impartiality and utmost rectitude."
translations.idiomatic: I wish to change at once the custom of mutual exaction above and below, and return to great impartiality and utmost rectitude."

sentences.zh: 帝親政，以直微猷閣知建甯府，明年，兼福建轉運判官。

translations.literal: When the Emperor personally took up government, he was made direct academician of the Weiyou Pavilion and prefect of Jianning; the next year he was given concurrent appointment as transport judge of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor personally took up government, he was made direct academician of the Weiyou Pavilion and prefect of Jianning; the next year he was given concurrent appointment as transport judge of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 閩鹽隸漕司，例運兩綱供費，後增至十有二，吏卒並緣爲奸，且抑州縣變賣，公私苦之，甫奏復舊例。

translations.literal: Min salt was under the transport commission; by precedent two shipments were sent for expenses, later increased to twelve; clerks and soldiers used this as a pretext for corruption and also suppressed prefectures and counties in forced sale—public and private all suffered; Fu memorialized to restore the old precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Min salt was under the transport commission; by precedent two shipments were sent for expenses, later increased to twelve; clerks and soldiers used this as a pretext for corruption and also suppressed prefectures in forced sale—public and private all suffered; Fu memorialized to restore the old precedent.

sentences.zh: 丁米錢久爲泉、漳、興化民患，會知漳州趙以夫請以廢寺租爲民代輸，甫並捐三郡歲解本司錢二萬七千貫助之。

translations.literal: The ding-rice money had long been a hardship for the people of Quan, Zhang, and Xinghua; it happened that the prefect of Zhangzhou Zhao Yifu requested using rent from abandoned temples to pay on the people's behalf; Fu also donated twenty-seven thousand strings of the three prefectures' annual payment to the commission to assist.
translations.idiomatic: The ding-rice money had long been a hardship for the people of Quan, Zhang, and Xinghua; when the prefect of Zhangzhou Zhao Yifu requested using rent from abandoned temples to pay on the people's behalf, Fu also donated twenty-seven thousand strings of the three prefectures' annual payment to the commission to assist.

sentences.zh: 郡屯左翼軍，本備峒寇，招捕司移之江西，甫檄使還營。

translations.literal: The prefecture garrisoned the Left Wing Army, originally to guard against cave bandits; the Pacification Office moved them to Jiangxi; Fu ordered them returned to camp.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture garrisoned the Left Wing Army, originally to guard against cave bandits; the Pacification Office moved them to Jiangxi; Fu ordered them returned to camp.

sentences.zh: 俄寇作唐石，即調之以行，而賊悉平。

translations.literal: Soon bandits arose at Tangshi; he immediately mobilized them on campaign and the bandits were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Soon bandits arose at Tangshi; he immediately mobilized them on campaign and the bandits were all pacified.

sentences.zh: 遷秘書少監。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice director of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice director of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 入見，帝曰：「卿久勞於外，篤意愛民，每覽所陳，備見懇惻。」

translations.literal: On audience the Emperor said: "You have long labored outside, with sincere intent to love the people; whenever I read what you submit, I see it is all earnest and sincere."
translations.idiomatic: On audience the Emperor said: "You have long labored outside, with sincere love for the people; whenever I read your memorials, I see they are all earnest and sincere."

sentences.zh: 甫奏《無逸》之義，言知農夫稼穡艱難，自然逸欲之念不起。

translations.literal: Fu presented the meaning of the "No Dissipation" chapter, saying that knowing the farmer's hardship in sowing and reaping naturally keeps dissolute desire from arising.
translations.idiomatic: Fu presented the meaning of the "No Dissipation" chapter, saying that knowing the farmer's hardship in sowing and reaping naturally keeps dissolute desire from arising.

sentences.zh: 乞力守更化以來求賢如不及之初意。

translations.literal: He begged to strive to uphold the initial intent since the reform of seeking the worthy as if one could not keep pace.
translations.idiomatic: He begged to strive to uphold the initial intent since the reform of seeking the worthy as if one could not keep pace.

sentences.zh: 遷起居舍人兼崇政殿說書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to attendant recorder with concurrent appointment as lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to attendant recorder with concurrent appointment as lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 於經筵奏：「剛之一字，最切于陛下。

translations.literal: In the classics lecture he memorialized: "The single word 'firm' is most urgent for Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: In the classics lecture he memorialized: "The single word 'firm' is most urgent for Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 陛下徒有慕漢宜厲精爲治之名，而乃墮元帝、文宗柔弱不振之失。

translations.literal: Your Majesty merely has the name of admiring Emperor Xuan of Han's resolve to govern with vigor, yet falls into the failures of Emperor Yuan and Emperor Wenzong—weak and unable to rouse.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty merely has the name of admiring Emperor Xuan of Han's resolve to govern with vigor, yet falls into the failures of Emperor Yuan and Emperor Wenzong—weak and unable to rouse.

sentences.zh: 元帝、文宗果斷，不用於斥邪佞，反用於逐賢人，此二君不識剛德之真。

translations.literal: Emperors Yuan and Wenzong were resolute, yet did not use it to expel evil flatterers but instead to drive out worthy men—these two rulers did not know the truth of firm virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Emperors Yuan and Wenzong were resolute, yet did not use it to expel evil flatterers but instead to drive out worthy men—these two rulers did not know the truth of firm virtue.

sentences.zh: 所謂真剛者，當爲之事必行，不當爲者則斷在勿行。」

translations.literal: What is called true firmness is that what ought to be done must be done, and what ought not must be decisively not done."
translations.idiomatic: What is called true firmness is that what ought to be done must be done, and what ought not must be decisively not done."

sentences.zh: 又乞「專意經訓，養育精神，務令充實，上與天一，下合人心。」

translations.literal: He also begged: "Concentrate on the classics, nurture the spirit, strive to make it full, above unite with heaven, below unite with the hearts of men."
translations.idiomatic: He also begged: "Concentrate on the classics, nurture the spirit, strive to make it full, above unite with heaven, below unite with the hearts of men."

sentences.zh: 帝意欲全功臣之世，詔自今中外臣僚奏事，毋得捃摭，以奏：「是消天下讜言之氣，其謂陛下何？」

translations.literal: The Emperor wished to protect the generations of meritorious families; an edict from now on forbade inner and outer officials, when memorializing, to gather and expose faults, to which he memorialized: "This extinguishes the spirit of forthright speech throughout the realm—what will they say of Your Majesty?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor wished to protect the generations of meritorious families; an edict forbade officials, when memorializing, to gather and expose faults, to which he memorialized: "This extinguishes forthright speech throughout the realm—what will they say of Your Majesty?"

sentences.zh: 兼中書舍人，繳奏不擿苛小，謂：「監司、郡守非其人，則一道一州之蠹也。」

translations.literal: With concurrent appointment as drafting secretary, he returned memorials and did not pick at petty harshness, saying: "If transport commissioners and prefects are not the right men, then a whole circuit or prefecture is their plague."
translations.idiomatic: With concurrent appointment as drafting secretary, he returned memorials and did not pick at petty harshness, saying: "If transport commissioners and prefects are not the right men, then a whole circuit or prefecture is their plague."

sentences.zh: 時相鄭清之以國用不足，履畝使輸券。

translations.literal: At the time the chief councilor Zheng Qingzhi, because state revenue was insufficient, sent field-measuring envoys to collect certificates.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the chief councilor Zheng Qingzhi, because state revenue was insufficient, sent field-measuring envoys to collect certificates.

sentences.zh: 甫奏：「避是虐賤，有力者頑未應令，而追呼迫促，破家蕩產，悲痛無聊者，大抵皆中下之戶。」

translations.literal: Fu memorialized: "Avoiding this oppresses the lowly; the powerful defy the order yet pursuit and summons are urgent, families ruined and property exhausted, grief and despair without relief—mostly these are middle and lower households."
translations.idiomatic: Fu memorialized: "Avoiding this oppresses the lowly; the powerful defy the order yet pursuit and summons are urgent, families ruined and property exhausted, grief and despair without relief—mostly these are middle and lower households."

sentences.zh: 嘗講罷，帝問近事，甫奏：「惟履畝事，人心最不悅。」

translations.literal: Once after lecture the Emperor asked about recent affairs; Fu memorialized: "Only the field-measuring matter—men's hearts are least pleased."
translations.idiomatic: Once after lecture the Emperor asked about recent affairs; Fu memorialized: "Only the field-measuring matter—men's hearts are least pleased."

sentences.zh: 又嘗讀《資治通鑒》，至漢高祖入關辭秦民牛酒，因奏：「今日無以予人，反橫科之，其心喜乎，怒乎？

translations.literal: He also once read the Comprehensive Mirror to the passage where Emperor Gaozu of Han on entering the pass declined the cattle and wine of Qin people, and memorialized: "Today there is nothing to give the people, yet levies are imposed across the board—are their hearts pleased or angry?
translations.idiomatic: He also once read the Comprehensive Mirror to the passage where Emperor Gaozu of Han on entering the pass declined the cattle and wine of Qin people, and memorialized: "Today there is nothing to give the people, yet levies are imposed across the board—are their hearts pleased or angry?

sentences.zh: 本朝立國以仁，陛下以爲此舉仁乎，否乎？」

translations.literal: Our dynasty founded the state on benevolence—does Your Majesty think this act benevolent or not?"
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty founded the state on benevolence—does Your Majesty think this act benevolent or not?"

sentences.zh: 帝爲惻然。

translations.literal: The Emperor was moved to compassion.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was moved to compassion.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷以邊事爲憂，史嵩之帥江西，力主和議。

translations.literal: At the time the court worried over border affairs; Shi Songzhi commanded Jiangxi and strongly advocated peace talks.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the court worried over border affairs; Shi Songzhi commanded Jiangxi and strongly advocated peace talks.

sentences.zh: 甫奏曰：「臣與嵩之居同裏，未嘗相知，而嵩之父彌忠，則與臣有故。

translations.literal: Fu memorialized: "Your servant and Songzhi live in the same village and have never been acquainted, yet Songzhi's father Mizhong and your servant have old ties.
translations.idiomatic: Fu memorialized: "Your servant and Songzhi live in the same village and have never been acquainted, yet Songzhi's father Mizhong and your servant have old ties.

sentences.zh: 嵩之易於主和，彌忠每戒其輕易。

translations.literal: Songzhi is quick to advocate peace; Mizhong always warned him against lightness.
translations.idiomatic: Songzhi is quick to advocate peace; Mizhong always warned him against lightness.

sentences.zh: 今朝廷甘心用父子異心之人，臣謂不特嵩之之易於主和，抑朝廷亦未免易於用人也。」

translations.literal: Now the court is content to employ a father and son of divided hearts—your servant says it is not only that Songzhi is quick to advocate peace, but that the court also cannot avoid being quick in employing men."
translations.idiomatic: Now the court is content to employ a father and son of divided hearts—your servant says it is not only that Songzhi is quick to advocate peace, but that the court also cannot avoid being quick in employing men."

sentences.zh: 疏入，不報。

translations.literal: The memorial entered and received no response.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial entered and received no response.

sentences.zh: 遂乞歸，不允。

translations.literal: He then begged to retire and was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He then begged to retire and was not permitted.

sentences.zh: 授起居郎兼中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was appointed attendant of the emperor's movements with concurrent drafting secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed attendant of the emperor's movements with concurrent drafting secretary.

sentences.zh: 未幾，擢嵩之刑部尚書，復奏疏云：「臣於嵩之本無仇怨，但國事所系，誼難緘默。」

translations.literal: Before long Songzhi was promoted to Minister of Justice; he again submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant has no enmity with Songzhi, but state affairs are involved and righteousness makes silence difficult."
translations.idiomatic: Before long Songzhi was promoted to Minister of Justice; he again submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant has no enmity with Songzhi, but state affairs are involved and righteousness makes silence difficult."

sentences.zh: 嵩之誥命，終不與書行，乃出甫知江州。

translations.literal: Songzhi's commission of appointment—he in the end would not draft it for issuance, and Fu was sent out as prefect of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Songzhi's commission of appointment—he in the end would not draft it for issuance, and Fu was sent out as prefect of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 王遂抗疏力爭，帝曰：「本以授其兄袁肅，報行誤耳。」

translations.literal: Wang Sui submitted a strenuous memorial in contention; the Emperor said: "It was originally to be given to his elder brother Yuan Su; the report of issuance was mistaken."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sui submitted a strenuous memorial in contention; the Emperor said: "It was originally to be given to his elder brother Yuan Su; the report of issuance was mistaken."

sentences.zh: 令遂勉甫無它志。

translations.literal: He ordered Sui to encourage Fu to have no other intent.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Sui to encourage Fu to have no other intent.

sentences.zh: 翼日，乃與肅江州。

translations.literal: The next day Su and Fu were both given Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Su and Fu were both given Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 而殿中侍御史徐清叟復論甫守富沙日贓六十萬，湯巾等又爭之，清叟亦悔。

translations.literal: But the palace attendant censor Xu Qingsou again impeached Fu for sixty myriad in embezzlement while prefect of Fusha; Tang Jin and others also contended; Qingsou also repented.
translations.idiomatic: But the palace attendant censor Xu Qingsou again impeached Fu for sixty myriad in embezzlement while prefect of Fusha; Tang Jin and others also contended; Qingsou also repented.

sentences.zh: 未幾，改知婺州，不拜。

translations.literal: Before long he was changed to prefect of Wuzhou and did not accept the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was changed to prefect of Wuzhou and did not accept the appointment.

sentences.zh: 遷兵部侍郎，入見，奏：「江潮暴湧，旱魃爲虐，楮幣蝕其心腹，大敵剝其四支，危亡之禍，近在旦夕，乞秉一德，塞邪徑。」

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice minister of War; on audience he memorialized: "The river tides surge violently, the drought demon wreaks havoc, paper currency eats at the heart and belly, the great enemy strips the four limbs—the calamity of peril and extinction is close at hand; I beg to hold to one virtue and block the evil path."
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice minister of War; on audience he memorialized: "The river tides surge violently, the drought demon wreaks havoc, paper currency eats at the heart and belly, the great enemy strips the four limbs—the calamity of peril and extinction is close at hand; I beg to hold to one virtue and block the evil path."

sentences.zh: 兼給事中。

translations.literal: With concurrent appointment as supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: With concurrent appointment as supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 岳珂以知兵財召，甫奏珂總餉二十年，焚林竭澤，珂竟從外補。

translations.literal: Yue Ke was summoned for knowledge of military finances; Fu memorialized that Ke had overseen supplies for twenty years, burning forests and draining marshes; Ke in the end was given an outer post.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Ke was summoned for knowledge of military finances; Fu memorialized that Ke had overseen supplies for twenty years, burning forests and draining marshes; Ke in the end was given an outer post.

sentences.zh: 遷吏部侍郎兼國子祭酒，日召諸生叩其問學理義講習之益。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice minister of Personnel with concurrent appointment as chancellor of the Directorate of Education, daily summoning students to inquire into the benefit of studying principles and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice minister of Personnel with concurrent appointment as chancellor of the Directorate of Education, daily summoning students to inquire into the benefit of studying principles and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 時邊遽日至，甫條十事，至爲詳明。

translations.literal: At the time border emergencies arrived daily; Fu set forth ten matters, extremely detailed and clear.
translations.idiomatic: At the time border emergencies arrived daily; Fu set forth ten matters, extremely detailed and clear.

sentences.zh: 權兵部尚書，暫兼吏部尚書，卒，贈通奉大夫，諡正肅。

translations.literal: He was given acting charge as minister of War, temporarily also minister of Personnel, died, and was posthumously made Grandee for Proper Service with the posthumous title Zhèngsù.
translations.idiomatic: He was given acting charge as minister of War, temporarily also minister of Personnel, died, and was posthumously made Grandee for Proper Service with the posthumous title Zhèngsù.

sentences.zh: 有《孝說》、《孟子解》、《後省封駁》、《信安志》、《江東荒政錄》、《防拓錄》、《樂事錄》及文集行世。

translations.literal: He had the Filial Piety Exposition, Explication of Mencius, Memorials Returned from the Rear Secretariat, Gazetteer of Xin'an, Record of Famine Administration in Jiangdong, Record of Frontier Defense, Record of Joyful Affairs, and collected works circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He left the Filial Piety Exposition, Explication of Mencius, Memorials Returned from the Rear Secretariat, Gazetteer of Xin'an, Record of Famine Administration in Jiangdong, Record of Frontier Defense, Record of Joyful Affairs, and collected works that circulated in his time.

sentences.zh: 甫少服父馴，謂學者當師聖人，以自得爲貴。

translations.literal: Fu in youth submitted to his father's discipline, saying scholars should take the sages as teachers and prize self-attainment.
translations.idiomatic: Fu in youth submitted to his father's discipline, saying scholars should take the sages as teachers and prize self-attainment.

sentences.zh: 又從楊簡問學，自謂「吾觀草木之發生，聽禽鳥之和鳴，與我心契，其樂無涯」云。

translations.literal: He also studied with Yang Jian, saying himself: "When I observe the sprouting of plants and trees, hear the harmonious cries of birds, and it accords with my heart—the joy is boundless," he said.
translations.idiomatic: He also studied with Yang Jian, saying himself: "When I observe the sprouting of plants and trees, hear the harmonious cries of birds, and it accords with my heart—the joy is boundless," he said.

sentences.zh: 劉黻，字聲伯，樂清人。

translations.literal: Liu Fu, style name Shengbo, was a native of Yueqing.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fu, courtesy name Shengbo, came from Yueqing.

sentences.zh: 早有令聞，讀書雁蕩山中僧寺。

translations.literal: He had an excellent reputation from youth and studied in a mountain monastery on Yandang.
translations.idiomatic: He had an excellent reputation from youth and studied in a mountain monastery on Yandang.

sentences.zh: 年三十四，以淳祐十年試入太學，儕輩已翕然稱之。

translations.literal: At age thirty-four, in the tenth year of Chunyou he entered the Imperial Academy by examination; his peers already spoke of him with one voice.
translations.idiomatic: At thirty-four, in the tenth year of Chunyou he entered the Imperial Academy by examination; his peers already spoke of him with one voice.

sentences.zh: 時丁大全方爲臺屬，劾奏丞相董槐，迫逐去國，將奪其位。

translations.literal: At the time Ding Daquan was a censorate staff officer; he impeached the chief councilor Dong Huai, forced him from office, and was about to seize his post.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Ding Daquan was a censorate staff officer; he impeached Chief Councilor Dong Huai, forced him from office, and was about to seize his post.

sentences.zh: 黻率同舍生伏闕上書，大概言朝廷進退大臣，須當以禮。

translations.literal: Fu led fellow students to prostrate themselves at the palace gate and submit a memorial, saying in summary that in advancing and dismissing great ministers the court must act according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Fu led fellow students to prostrate themselves at the palace gate and submit a memorial, saying in summary that in advancing and dismissing great ministers the court must act according to ritual.

sentences.zh: 書上，忤執政，送南安軍安置，歸別其母解氏。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted it offended those in power; he was sent to Nan'an Circuit for resettlement and returned to bid farewell to his mother, the Lady Xie.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted it offended those in power; he was sent to Nan'an Circuit for resettlement and returned to bid farewell to his mother, Lady Xie.

sentences.zh: 解氏曰：「爲臣死忠，以直被貶，分也。

translations.literal: Lady Xie said: "As a minister, die loyal; to be demoted for uprightness is one's portion.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xie said: "As a minister, die loyal; to be demoted for uprightness is one's portion.

sentences.zh: 速行！」

translations.literal: Go quickly!"
translations.idiomatic: Go quickly!"

sentences.zh: 黻至南安，盡取濂、洛諸子之書，摘其精切之語，輯成書十卷，名曰《濂洛論語》。

translations.literal: When Fu reached Nan'an he took all the books of the Lian and Luo masters, selected their most essential passages, and compiled them into ten juan titled Discourses of Lian and Luo.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu reached Nan'an he took all the books of the Lian and Luo masters, selected their most essential passages, and compiled them into ten juan titled Discourses of Lian and Luo.

sentences.zh: 及大全貶，黻還太學。

translations.literal: When Daquan was demoted, Fu returned to the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: When Daquan was demoted, Fu returned to the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 未幾，侍御史陳垓誣劾程公許，右正言蔡滎誣劾黃之純，二公罷出，六館相顧失色，黻又率諸生上書言：

translations.literal: Before long the attendant censor Chen Gai falsely impeached Cheng Gongxu, and the right rectifier Cai Ying falsely impeached Huang Zhichun; both were dismissed and left office; the six halls looked at one another in dismay; Fu again led the students in submitting a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Before long Attendant Censor Chen Gai falsely impeached Cheng Gongxu, and Right Rectifier Cai Ying falsely impeached Huang Zhichun; both were dismissed; the six halls looked at one another in dismay; Fu again led the students in submitting a memorial saying:

sentences.zh: 黻等蒙被教養，視國家休戚利害若己痛養。

translations.literal: Fu and others have received your teaching and nurture; we regard the state's weal and woe, benefit and harm, as our own pain and nourishment.
translations.idiomatic: Fu and others have received your teaching and nurture; we regard the state's weal and woe as our own pain and nourishment.

sentences.zh: 朝廷進一君子，台諫發一公論，則彈冠相慶，喜溢肺膺。

translations.literal: When the court advances one gentleman and the censorate and remonstrance bureaus issue one public judgment, then we adjust our caps and rejoice together, joy overflowing in our breasts.
translations.idiomatic: When the court advances one gentleman and the censorate issues one public judgment, we adjust our caps and rejoice together, joy overflowing in our breasts.

sentences.zh: 至若君子郁而不獲用，公論沮而不克伸，則憂憤忡結，寢食俱廢。
